newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria, Iran condemn U.S. veto, say harms peace.
newsitem.headline: Syria, Iran condemn U.S. veto, say harms peace.

text.p: Syria and Iran on Sunday strongly condemned the United States for vetoing a U.N. draft resolution calling on Israel to abandon plans to build a new Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem.

Both Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara and Iran's Ali Akbar Velayati said Washington's move did not come as a surprise because the United States had always supported Israel's "expansionist" actions.

"The U.S. veto will not help efforts aimed at pushing the peace process forward. The U.S. justification for blocking the draft is not convincing," Shara said while welcoming Velayati on arrival in Damascus.
Velayati said the U.S. veto was "a lesson for the Islamic countries which attach hopes on others and a motive for them to rally their resources to liberate Jerusalem."
Velayati, who came to Syria to convey an invitation to President Hafez al-Assad to attend the Islamic conference in Iran in December, said Moslem states should hold high-level talks over Jerusalem.

The United States, as one of the permanent members of the U.N. Security Council, killed the resolution by its negative vote on Friday following a council debate on Israel's plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews in East Jerusalem captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
All other 14 members of the Security Council voted in favour of the resolution, drafted by Britain, France, Portugal and Sweden.
Shara praised the European Union for drafting the resolution and described as "fair" Europe's position regarding the Middle East peace process.

"The U.S. veto was not surprising for us because the United States has been for some time trying to block the Security Council from taking any position regarding the Israeli aggressive and expansionist policies," Shara said.
"The U.S. veto is denounced by the Arab and Islamic world. I add that the U.S. veto was used against a European draft and this is a precedent which should be taken into consideration."
Shara added that the U.S. veto would encourage Israel to "violate international law" and build more settlements in occupied Arab lands. He said he hoped Washington would reconsider its position.

The United States is the main sponsor of Israel's peace talks with Arabs including Syria whose negotiations with the Jewish state broke off a year ago. Syria supports a greater European role in the negotiations.
The Syrian-Israeli talks are stalled over the fate of the Golan Heights, a strategic plateau captured by Israel in 1967.
